scenes.tts: How does an immune protein mark something to be eaten? And does the young brain use the same trick?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Tag and a Reader. A synapse beside a bacterium, both with question marks.
scenes.narration: How does an immune protein mark something to be eaten? And does the young brain use the same trick?

scenes.tts: In the blood, complement marks targets for eating cells. Three steps matter here.
scenes.visual: A three-step strip appears, empty: 1 binds, 2 cut and stick, 3 read.
scenes.narration: In the blood, complement marks targets for eating cells. Three steps matter here.

scenes.tts: Step one. C one q binds. It is shaped like a bunch of six tulips, and each head can grip a surface.
scenes.visual: C1q drawn as six heads on stalks, landing on a surface. Step 1 lights.
scenes.caption: Step one. C1q binds. It is shaped like a bunch of six tulips, and each head can grip a surface.
scenes.narration: Step one. C1q binds. It is shaped like a bunch of six tulips, and each head can grip a surface.

scenes.tts: Step two. Enzymes in the C one q complex cut two more proteins. Their pieces build an enzyme that cuts C three.
scenes.visual: A single cut animation: two proteins, labelled small as C4 and C2, split and assemble into a C3-cutting enzyme. Step 2 lights.
scenes.caption: Step two. Enzymes in the C1q complex cut two more proteins. Their pieces build an enzyme that cuts C3.
scenes.narration: Step two. Enzymes in the C1q complex cut two more proteins. Their pieces build an enzyme that cuts C3.

scenes.tts: C three splits in two. The large piece, C three b, can fix itself to the nearby surface.
scenes.visual: C3 splits into a small C3a, which drifts off, and a large C3b, which staples to the surface.
scenes.caption: C3 splits in two. The large piece, C3b, can fix itself to the nearby surface.
scenes.narration: C3 splits in two. The large piece, C3b, can fix itself to the nearby surface.

scenes.tts: Step three. C three b is trimmed to i C three b. Complement receptor three, on an eating cell, binds it, which promotes engulfment.
scenes.visual: C3b trims to iC3b; a phagocyte process carrying complement receptor 3 (CR3) reaches and binds it. Step 3 lights.
scenes.caption: Step three. C3b is trimmed to iC3b. Complement receptor 3, on an eating cell, binds it, which promotes engulfment.
scenes.narration: Step three. C3b is trimmed to iC3b. Complement receptor 3, on an eating cell, binds it, which promotes engulfment.

scenes.tts: Now to neurons. Beth Stevens, in Ben Barres's laboratory, grew purified retinal ganglion cells with astrocytes in a dish. The neurons raised their C one q.
scenes.visual: Credit: Stevens, in the Barres laboratory, Stanford. A dish with retinal ganglion cells and astrocytes; a C1q label brightens in the neurons.
scenes.caption: Now to neurons. Beth Stevens, in Ben Barres's laboratory, grew purified retinal ganglion cells with astrocytes in a dish. The neurons raised their C1q.
scenes.narration: Now to neurons. Beth Stevens, in Ben Barres's laboratory, grew purified retinal ganglion cells with astrocytes in a dish. The neurons raised their C1q.

scenes.tts: In the young mouse visual thalamus, C one q and C three lay at developing synapses.
scenes.visual: Synapses in the dLGN with C1q and C3 dots on them.
scenes.caption: In the young mouse visual thalamus, C1q and C3 lay at developing synapses.
scenes.narration: In the young mouse visual thalamus, C1q and C3 lay at developing synapses.

scenes.tts: One caution. Neurons can make C one q, but most brain C one q comes from microglia. Which cell supplies it at these synapses is not settled.
scenes.visual: Caution card: most brain C1q comes from microglia; the source at dLGN synapses is not settled.
scenes.caption: One caution. Neurons can make C1q, but most brain C1q comes from microglia. Which cell supplies it at these synapses is not settled.
scenes.narration: One caution. Neurons can make C1q, but most brain C1q comes from microglia. Which cell supplies it at these synapses is not settled.

scenes.tts: Predict. If complement helps remove losing inputs, what should a mouse without C one q look like?
scenes.visual: Question card over two blank dLGN outlines: normal and C1q knockout.
scenes.caption: Predict. If complement helps remove losing inputs, what should a mouse without C1q look like?
scenes.narration: Predict. If complement helps remove losing inputs, what should a mouse without C1q look like?

scenes.tts: The two eyes' territories failed to refine normally. They still overlapped more than in normal littermates.
scenes.visual: Genotype panel: normal, red and blue separate; C1q knockout, a wide purple overlap zone. Schematic.
scenes.narration: The two eyes' territories failed to refine normally. They still overlapped more than in normal littermates.

scenes.tts: Single relay neurons agreed. Most knockout cells still received several inputs, where normal cells had few.
scenes.visual: Two relay neurons: normal with one or two inputs; knockout with several. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Single relay neurons agreed. Most knockout cells still received several inputs, where normal cells had few.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking C three showed a similar overlap.
scenes.visual: A third panel, C3 knockout, with a purple overlap zone like the C1q knockout.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking C3 showed a similar overlap.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking C3 showed a similar overlap.

scenes.tts: What this shows: complement is needed for normal refinement in this circuit.
scenes.visual: Card: shown, complement is needed for refinement here.
scenes.narration: What this shows: complement is needed for normal refinement in this circuit.

scenes.tts: What it does not show: which synapse got a tag, what read it, or which cell carried the input away.
scenes.visual: Three question marks: which synapse? what read it? which cell?
scenes.narration: What it does not show: which synapse got a tag, what read it, or which cell carried the input away.

scenes.tts: So the knockouts point to a tag. The next step is to catch the eater in the act.
scenes.visual: Closing card: a tag, and an empty space for the eater.
scenes.narration: So the knockouts point to a tag. The next step is to catch the eater in the act.
